rules.title: Rules of CodeVerse Hub
rules.content:
**R1❯ Follow Discord Terms & Guidelines**

All server rules are based on Discord’s Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.
Modded clients like Vencord or BetterDiscord are allowed.

**R2❯ No Raids, Doxxing, or Swatting**

Do not participate in, joke about, or threaten raids, doxxing, or swatting.
Any such threat will result in a permanent ban.
Sharing information related to these actions is also prohibited, even “for awareness”.
You may discuss incidents for awareness only, without encouraging the behavior.

**R3❯ No Scams, Malware, or Malicious Links**

Using Discord for scams, malware, viruses, IP grabbers, or harmful links is strictly prohibited.
This applies both inside the server and in DMs.
Cybersecurity discussions are allowed only in appropriate channels.
Do not share malware, source code, tutorials, tools, or stream such content.

**R4❯ No Sharing Personal Information**

Leaking or sharing personal information is not allowed.
This includes IP addresses, phone numbers, addresses, legal names, IDs, or similar data.

**R5❯ Voice Channel Conduct**

Prohibited behavior in voice channels includes:
Racism, sexism, hate speech, ToS violations, earrape, or disruptive behavior.
Recording or archiving conversations without owner permission is not allowed.

**R6❯ No NSFW, Gore, or Shock Content**

NSFW content, gore, shock content, or explicit behavior is strictly prohibited.
This includes jokes or indirect references to such content.
Racism and sexism are also not allowed.

**R7❯ No Politics or Religious Debates**

Politics and religion are not topics for this server.
Any offensive content toward countries, institutions, or beliefs is prohibited.
Any reference to Nazis/Hitler or equivalents will result in a permanent ban.

**R8❯ Profiles Must Follow Rules**

Your Discord profile must comply with server rules and Discord ToS.
Names, bios, avatars, pronouns, and statuses can be moderated.
NSFW content, hate speech, impersonation, or malicious content will be punished.

**R9❯ No Advertising**

Advertising is not allowed on this server.
DM advertising without a valid reason is prohibited and can result in a ban.
If someone asks for a link, share it via DM only.
Projects may be shared only in the appropriate channels.

**R10❯ No Rule Loopholes / Use Common Sense**

These rules are not exhaustive.
Trying to bypass rules is not allowed.
If unsure, ask staff via tickets or do not proceed.

**R11❯ Respect Moderation Decisions**

Do not disrupt the server if you disagree with a punishment.
Appeal respectfully through proper channels.
If bias is suspected after appeal, contact staff in this order via tickets/modmail only:
Head Mod → Admin → Owner
Do not DM staff or add them without consent.

**TL;DR**
Use common sense, respect others, and act maturely.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.content:
### Staff & Roles

**Q: How do I become a Helper or Moderator?**
We do not have public applications for staff roles. Members are nominated by existing staff based on their helpfulness, activity, and adherence to our culture. If you are active and helpful, you might be noticed!

**Q: What do the roles mean?**
Check out our [Server Information](/pages/server-info) page for a breakdown of all roles.

### Bots

**Q: Can I get @CodeVerseBot on my server?**
Currently, our bot is specific to our server architecture and is not open for public invites. However, the source code is available on our GitHub if you wish to host your own instance.

**Q: Who is @ModMail?**
ModMail is a bot that allows you to send private messages to the staff team. Simply DM the bot to open a ticket.

### Server Questions

**Q: Why can't I upload files?**
We restrict file uploads to ensure safety. Please use paste services like [Pastebin](https://pastebin.com) or GitHub Gists for code sharing.

**Q: Can I advertise my project?**
Specific advertising is generally not allowed to prevent spam. You may showcase open-source projects in the designated `#showcase` channel if they are relevant to the community.

### Misc

**Q: Is this server official?**
We are a community-run server dedicated to coding and development. We are not affiliated with any official organization.

**Q: How can I suggest features or improvements?**
Feel free to open a discussion in the `#suggestions` channel or contact staff via ModMail. We welcome constructive feedback!

resources.title: Learning Resources
resources.content:
These resources are recommended by the CodeVerse Hub community helping you on your coding journey!

### General & Beginner Friendly

*   **[Automate the Boring Stuff with Python](https://automatetheboringstuff.com/)**: One of the best books out there for Python beginners. Teaches basics and automation.
*   **[CS50P: Introduction to Programming with Python](https://cs50.harvard.edu/python/2022/)**: Harvard's free self-paced course. Highly recommended.
*   **[Python Crash Course](https://nostarch.com/pythoncrashcourse2e)**: A fast-paced, thorough introduction to programming.
*   **[Real Python](https://realpython.com/)**: A treasure trove of quizzes, tutorials, and content for learning Python.
*   **[MDN Web Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/)**: The definitive resource for Web Development (HTML, CSS, JS).
*   **[The Odin Project](https://www.theodinproject.com/)**: A Full Stack Web Development curriculum.

### Intermediate & Advanced

*   **[Fluent Python](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/fluent-python/9781491946237/)**: A must-read for any Python professional. Deep dives into Python's internals.
*   **[Effective Python](https://effectivepython.com/)**: 90 best practices for writing excellent Python code.
*   **[Software Design by Example](https://third-bit.com/sdxpy/)**: A tool-based introduction to Software Design.

### Data Science & Machine Learning

*   **[Data Science from Scratch](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/data-science-from/9781492041122/)**: A good introduction to data science for the complete beginner.
*   **[Kaggle Pandas Tutorial](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/pandas)**: Interactive tutorial for learning Pandas.
*   **[Neural Networks from Scratch](https://nnfs.io/)**: Build neural networks from scratch to understand deep learning from the ground up.
*   **[Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/)**: Run code in the cloud with GPU support, great for ML experiments.

### Tools & Editors

*   **[VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/)**: A fully-featured editor, extendable with plugins. Most popular choice.
*   **[PyCharm](https://www.jetbrains.com/pycharm/)**: The very best Python IDE with advanced features.
*   **[Git Guide](https://rogerdudler.github.io/git-guide/)**: A simple, no-nonsense guide to using Git.
*   **[Regex101](https://regex101.com/)**: An online tool for testing regular expressions.

### Interactive Learning

*   **[Exercism](https://exercism.org/)**: Level up skills with mentored code exercises.
*   **[Python Tutor](https://www.pythontutor.com/)**: Visualize code execution step-by-step.
*   **[Code Combat](https://codecombat.com/)**: Learn Python while gaming through an RPG.

### Video Tutorials

*   **[Corey Schafer](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCCezIgC97PvUuR4_gbFUs5g)**: High-quality tutorials on Python, Django, Flask, and more.
*   **[Sentdex](https://www.youtube.com/user/sentdex)**: Enormous amount of Python content for all skill levels.
*   **[Microsoft Developer](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCsMica-v34Irf9KVTh6xx-g)**: High-quality Python tutorials for beginners from Microsoft.

*Note: This list is curated from various successful developer communities.*

tags.title: Useful Tags & Snippets
tags.content:
These are some of the most commonly used tags in our server. You can trigger them using our bot commands.

### General Python

**args-kwargs**
These special parameters allow functions to take arbitrary amounts of positional (`*args`) and keyword (`**kwargs`) arguments. The names are convention, but the asterisks are what matter.

**async-await**
Python provides the ability to run multiple tasks and coroutines simultaneously with the use of the `asyncio` library. This is crucial for Discord bots to remain responsive.

**codeblock**
Please use codeblocks when sharing code! 
\`\`\`python
print("Hello World")
\`\`\`
This makes your code readable and colorful.

**pep8**
PEP 8 is the official style guide for Python. It includes guidelines for naming variables (`snake_case`), classes (`CamelCase`), and formatting code to be readable.

**venv (Virtual Environments)**
Always use a virtual environment for your projects! It keeps dependencies isolated.
`python -m venv .venv`

### Discord.py / Nextcord

**intents**
Intents are a feature of Discord that tells the gateway exactly which events to send your bot. You must enable them in the Developer Portal and in your code.

**cogs**
Cogs allow you to organize your bot's commands into different files (classes). This is essential for keeping large bots maintainable.

### Common Pitfalls

**mutable-default-args**
Avoid using mutable objects (like lists or dicts) as default arguments in functions. They are created only *once* when the function is defined, not every time it runs.

**xy-problem**
Please ask about your *actual problem*, not just the solution you are attempting. Often there is a better way to solve the root issue.

moderation-guide.title: Moderation Guide
moderation-guide.content:
Our moderation team is committed to keeping the community safe. If you see a violation, please report it.

### Reporting Violations

To report a rule violation:
1.  **Open a ModMail ticket:** DM the @ModMail bot with details of the incident.
2.  **Provide evidence:** Include screenshots, message links, or any relevant context.
3.  **Be respectful:** Keep your report factual and avoid emotional language.

### Handling Reports

Moderators should:
1.  **Review the evidence:** Carefully examine the provided information.
2.  **Consult the rules:** Ensure the reported behavior clearly violates our rules.
3.  **Take action:** Issue warnings, temporary bans, or permanent bans as appropriate.
4.  **Document actions:** Keep records of all moderation actions for future reference.

### Appeals Process

Users may appeal moderation actions by:
1.  **Opening a ModMail ticket:** Explain why they believe the action was unjust.
2.  **Providing context:** Include any relevant information or evidence.
3.  **Waiting for review:** The moderation team will review the appeal and respond accordingly.

code-of-conduct.title: CodeVerse Hub Code of Conduct
code-of-conduct.content:
This document outlines the expectations for participation in the CodeVerse Hub community. We are dedicated to providing a friendly, safe, and welcoming environment for everyone, regardless of experience level, gender, sexual orientation, disability, personal appearance, race, ethnicity, age, religion, or nationality.

### Our Goal

The purpose of this Code of Conduct is to set the tone for our community. It is not an exhaustive list of do's and don'ts, but rather a guide to help us all be our best selves. We value collaboration and support just as much as technical expertise. Helping others and fostering a positive environment is highly encouraged.

### Scope

This Code of Conduct applies to all spaces managed by CodeVerse Hub, including our Discord server, GitHub organization, and any other platforms we operate. It applies to all members, including staff.

### Expected Behavior

Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment include:

*   **Be kind and courteous:** Treat everyone with respect and kindness.
*   **Use inclusive language:** Ensure your words welcome everyone.
*   **Respect differing viewpoints:** We all come from different backgrounds; listen and learn from each other.
*   **Collaborate:** Work together and support fellow members.
*   **Accept criticism gracefully:** Use feedback to improve and grow.
*   **Prioritize the community:** Act in the best interest of CodeVerse Hub.
*   **Show empathy:** Understand and relate to the feelings of others.

### Unacceptable Behavior

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

*   **Harassment:** Public or private harassment of any kind.
*   **Inappropriate Content:** Sexualized language/imagery, or inappropriate avatars/nicknames.
*   **Disruptive Behavior:** Trolling, spamming, flaming, baiting, or attention-seeking.
*   **Attacks:** Insults, derogatory comments, or personal/political attacks.
*   **Doxxing:** Publishing others' private information without permission.
*   **Polarizing Topics:** Discussing sensitive or inflammatory subjects (politics, violence, etc.) that incite arguments.
*   **Unhelpful Responses:** dismissive replies like "Just Google it" or "RTFM" to help requests.

### Moderation Policy

CodeVerse Hub's moderation team (Moderators, Admins, Owners) enforces this Code of Conduct and our Community Rules.

1.  **Enforcement:** Staff have the authority to address any behavior they deem inappropriate, even if not explicitly listed here.
2.  **No Public Complaints:** Do not argue about moderation actions in public channels. If you disagree with a decision, please open a ticket or DM ModMail.
3.  **Appeals:** You may appeal moderation decisions through the proper channels detailed below.

### Reporting Violations

If you witness or experience a violation of this Code of Conduct, please report it immediately. You can do so by:

*   Opening a **ModMail** ticket on our Discord server.
*   Tagging the `@Moderators` role for urgent issues (use sparingly).
*   Emailing us at `thecodeversedev@gmail.com` for sensitive matters.

### Consequences of Unacceptable Behavior

Unacceptable behavior will not be tolerated. Consequences may include:

*   **Warning:** A formal warning about the behavior.
*   **Temporary Ban:** A temporary removal from the community.
*   **Permanent Ban:** A permanent removal from the community.

### Appeals Process

If you believe a moderation action was unjust, you may appeal by following these steps:

1.  **Open a Ticket:** Use ModMail to open a ticket explaining your case.
2.  **Provide Details:** Include any relevant context or evidence.
3.  **Wait for Review:** The moderation team will review your appeal and respond accordingly.

### Acknowledgment

By participating in CodeVerse Hub, you agree to abide by this Code of Conduct. We reserve the right to update this document as needed to ensure a safe and welcoming environment for all members.

privacy-policy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy-policy.content:
### Introduction

This document details what data CodeVerse Hub refers to as "we", "us", or "our" stores on you as a member of our community. Privacy and security of member data is one of our top priorities.

### What data do we store?

*   **User Information:** We store Discord User IDs, usernames, and discriminators to identify you across our services.
*   **Infraction Records:** When a user breaches our rules, we store a record of the infraction (warn/ban/kick) linked to their User ID. This is essential for moderation history.
*   **ModMail logs:** All messages sent to our ModMail bot are stored to facilitate support and moderation oversight.
*   **Message Logs:** We do not permanently store general chat logs. However, deleted messages may be temporarily logged for moderation review.

### Assurance on Processing

*   **Data Minimization:** We only store data that is critical to the operation of our community and safety of our members.
*   **Access Control:** Direct access to the database is limited to the Owner. Infraction and ModMail data is accessible to Moderators and Admins strictly for moderation purposes.

### Your Rights

*   **Access:** You may request a copy of the data we hold on you by contacting us.
*   **Deletion:** You may request deletion of your data. We will comply unless the data is required for moderation purposes (e.g., active ban records).

### Contact

For privacy concerns, please contact us via ModMail or email `thecodeversedev@gmail.com`.

security-notice.title: Security Notice
security-notice.content:
### Reporting a Vulnerability

If you've found a vulnerability in any CodeVerse Hub project, we would like to know so we can fix it before it is exploited.

**Please do NOT open a public GitHub issue for security vulnerabilities.**

Send details to `thecodeversedev@gmail.com` or DM a server Admin, including:

*   The website, page, or repository where the vulnerability can be observed.
*   A brief description of the vulnerability.
*   Non-destructive exploitation details.

### Scope

The following are **NOT** in scope:

*   Volumetric vulnerabilities (e.g. DDOS).
*   Reports indicating missing security headers without a proof of concept.
*   Social engineering attacks.

We will do our best to reply as fast as possible.

server-info.title: Server Information
server-info.content:
### Staff Roles

*   **Owner:** Reviews high-level appeals, manages infrastructure, and direction.
*   **Admin:** Oversees the moderation team and maintains bots/services.
*   **Moderator:** Enforces rules, handles tickets, and keeps the community safe.
*   **Helper:** Community members recognized for their technical expertise and willingness to help others throughout the server.

### Community Roles

*   **Contributor:** Awarded to those who have contributed code to our open source projects.
*   **Booster:** A cosmetic role for those who boost the server.
*   **Member:** The heart of our community!

### Bots

*   **@CodeVerseBot:** Our custom bot handling utility and simple moderation tasks.
*   **@ModMail:** Send a DM to this bot to open a private ticket with staff.

guides.title: Guides
guides.content:
Helpful guides for members of the CodeVerse Hub community.

### Asking Good Questions
To get the best help possible, follow these steps:
1.  **Search first:** Check Google and previous chats.
2.  **Be specific:** "It doesn't work" is not helpful. detailed error messages and code snippets are.
3.  **Show your code:** Use codeblocks.
4.  **Provide context:** What are you trying to achieve?

### Contributing to Open Source
We love open source! If you want to contribute to our projects:
*   Check the GitHub Issues tab for "Good First Issues".
*   Fork the repository.
*   Create a new branch.
*   Submit a Pull Request (PR).

### setting up a Dev Environment
1.  Install Git.
2.  Install VS Code.
3.  Install the language runtime (Node.js, Python, etc.).
4.  Clone the repo!
